newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: European Leisure sets 2-for-3 rights issue.
newsitem.headline: European Leisure sets 2-for-3 rights issue.

text.p: European Leisure on Tuesday announced a two-for-three rights issue at 145 pence per share to raise 11.4 million sterling net of expenses.
The proceeds of the issue, which is fully underwritten by Charterhouse Bank Ltd, will be used primarily to fund a focused expansion programme, European Leisure said in a statement.
The company also announced the early conversion of preference shares owned by its banking syndicate into new ordinary shares which will be placed with institutional investors at 145 pence per share.
A further 1.8 million shares owned by members of the banking syndicate will also be placed taking the gross value of the placing to 20.3 million sterling.
As a result, the banking syndicates' interest in the company will fall to 11 percent from 67 percent.

European Leisure also announced the early redemption of 2.5 million convertible loan notes at a 10 percent discount from the proceeds of the rights issue while it plans an early repayment of three million pounds of debt in April 1997 out of trading cash flows.
The group said proforma gearing fell to 56 percent at June 30, 1996, from 85 percent as a result of the proposals.
The company also plans to pay a dividend on its ordinary shares in respect of the year ending June 30, 1997 in the absence of unforseen circumstances.

European Leisure is one of the largest operators of discotheques in the UK with some 42 sites located throughout the country and also owns 54 snooker clubs. Its portfolio includes venues such as the Hippodrome and the Camden Palace.
It said it believed opportunities existed for expansion through the selective acquisition of further venues and the continued development and refurbishment of existing sites.
"The board believes full advantage can be taken of the proposed relaxation in licensing laws and the consequential change in leisure habits by increasing the group's portfolio of venue bars."
European Leisure said it was optimistic about future trading prospects and trading since the half-year stage was ahead of the same period last year.
